items.text: the speaker is the master mute. Tap it and what you hear goes quiet while the sound plays on (its wave still moves); scenes and Auto play can no longer turn it back on, only you can. Hold it for the shelf, to stop or change the sound
in Auto play, Changes are checkboxes: Pattern, Style and Sound, with Scene across the top for all three. Untick Sound and the music carries on across the changes
the bead that times the next scene wears a ring that fills up to it; dim when the dice picked it, a step per beat when counting beats or bars
the dice in Every is the same dice as the Random button
Touchable sound is six icon tiles (Fader, Sweep, Pan, Wash, Tide, and Mapping with Pro); point at one, or tap it, and its sentence shows in one line at the foot
Paths wears a scholar's hat, so it reads as learning: on the cover, in the index and on the suggestions card. Walk every path and the hat becomes a ribbon
on a computer, panels no longer float, pin or drag. Each opens in its own place and closes as before, until a proper desktop system arrives: one pane on the right that holds them all
with a mouse, the caret now shows over ▶ too, saying the scenes and Auto play open above it; a click on the caret opens them, as on the other buttons
at the foot of Auto play, a Scenes in play button with the count beside it (12 of 35); the button opens Scenes, where you tick them in or out
on a slow connection the duck-rabbit could load twice: it landed, then filled up with colour again. It now arrives once, already in colour
Auto play's Every is a row of beads with the count inside; count in seconds, beats or bars, or pick the dice bead for a random length each time. Beats and bars follow the beat that plays
Changes shows the whole scene across the top and its two halves, pattern and style, under it; the whole scene lights both
counts sit at each tile's top right, morph times too; a Pro feature shows a lock, a dotted edge and a faint tint
